summary: The note argues that small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can compete for skilled talent by leveraging flatter hierarchies, strong workplace culture, investment in professional development, technology adoption, and partnerships with educational institutions. It cites several experts and a Global SME Culture Survey to support these points. The note ends without a conclusion.
one_line: SMEs can win skilled talent through distinctive culture, development investment, technology, and education partnerships rather than competing on corporate prestige.
key_facts: As of September 2023, the labor market has shifted due to technological advancements, evolving employee expectations, and fierce competition.
SMEs typically have flatter hierarchies, enabling closer interaction between employees, management, and business owners.
Carolyn Brighton, a talent acquisition consultant, says SME employees can directly see the impact of their work on business outcomes, which is a powerful motivator.
The Global SME Culture Survey, published on October 17, 2023, found that 58% of respondents ranked workplace culture as a top three priority when considering a job offer.
James Keller, CEO of TechInnovate, said the company struggled with high turnover until it built a strong, values-driven culture that puts employees first, which drastically improved retention.

Jane McConnell, an expertise development manager at a midsize manufacturing firm, says a dedicated professional development budget makes prospects see the firm as a career destination rather than a stepping stone.
The note recommends SMEs tailor training to both business needs and individual employee aspirations.
Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) can streamline onboarding, performance management, and employee self-service portals.
David Hansen, a leading SME digital strategist, advises seeing technology as an ally in attracting skilled talent by improving work-life quality and simplifying processes.
Collaborative apprenticeships, internships, and certification programs with educational institutions, professional associations, and industry groups can bring fresh talent and skills to SMEs.
Midco Enterprises partnered with a local technical college, and its annual report describes how graduates brought new energy and expertise to its R&D department.
The note's conclusion section is left empty, marked as 'No conclusion as per the request'.
